$comment: Who may read and write each model of prisma/schema/numbering.prisma (rules: src/ownership.ts; roles: src/roles.ts). Document numbers (NumberSeries, NumberAllocation) are issued by apps/factory-api's allocateNumber inside an office (or worker) command; floor and portal sessions get no grant on them, so a tablet can never move a company's counter (a fiscal one least of all). Scan ids (BUNDLE, HIDE, GARMENT_SERIAL) are the floor's numbers: a tablet takes a block of them (online, or for itself to number offline) and records the numbers it used; the …_numbering_floor_guards triggers hold that a block starts above every block before it, is never changed but closed, and that a used number lies in an open block of its tablet. NumberAllocation and NumberBlockUse are append-only (`@append-only`, scripts/factory/check-append-only.mjs): no update or delete grant, and their triggers refuse UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE for every login. Series and blocks are closed, never deleted. After a change run `npm run policies -w @nexus/factory-db -- <folder>`.

NumberSeries.about: Office sessions and the worker keep the series: an admin creates one, sets its start or moves it past a number (numbering.manage, through command()), and allocateNumber locks the row and moves its counter. The API keeps staff to the companies their grants reach (scopeWhere / can()).

NumberAllocation.about: Office sessions and the worker add one row per issued number (allocateNumber) and read the ledger (which record has which number; the no-gap check). Nobody changes or removes a row.

NumberBlock.about: The tenant's ledger of scan-id blocks: the counter of each scan-id kind is its highest toRef. Office sessions and the worker take blocks (allocateScanIds online; a tablet's block from the office's screen), read them and close one (a lost or retired tablet: the only update the guard allows). Floor sessions take blocks too (online numbers for their own commands, their tablet's top-up) and read the tenant's whole ledger: a row holds only references, a kind and a device id, and the counter is tenant-wide. No site key: a block is the tenant's, not a site's row.

NumberBlockUse.about: The numbers a tablet used from its blocks. Floor sessions add them inside their own command (useScanIds) and read their site's; office sessions and the worker read them and may add them for a tablet (a system command acting for it). Nobody changes or removes a row.
